---
title: "SEO strategy across Tuturuuu"
description: "Search intent, canonical ownership, product and docs content, privacy, localization, and measurable outcomes."
updatedAt: '2026-10-08'
---

## Goals and audience

Help someone discover the appropriate product, understand a concrete workflow,
verify the implementation contract, and start an eligible workspace experience.
Keep private content out of search. Measure qualified discovery and successful
onboarding rather than treating raw indexed URL count as the goal.

| Search intent | Canonical content | Next useful destination |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tuturuuu identity and capabilities | Web homepage, about, product directory | Product page and docs getting started |
| Tasks/calendar/time planning | Web Tasks/Calendar/Track pages | App guide, scheduling rules, private app entry |
| CRM/forms/business operations | Web CRM/Forms/Finance/Inventory pages | App guide, permission and publishing details |
| Shopping for a published product | Owning Storefront product page | Store/cart; private checkout stays unindexed |
| Learning a subject or tool | Nova public lessons, Tools pages, docs learning guides | Relevant practice or authenticated product |
| Creating and discovering worlds | Tulletin landing, public explorer, published world | Creator content and authorized private studio |
| Integrating or operating Tuturuuu | Docs SDK/API/package/runtime guides | Source-derived route/version references |

## Own one public URL per purpose

Web owns broad product and solution descriptions. The satellite owns the usable
public tool or published content when it serves one. Docs owns learning and
integration contracts. Link these together with meaningful labels rather than
copying the same landing page onto every host. Preserve redirect aliases when
moving a public page; update canonicals, internal links, and sitemap ownership
together.

Every indexable page needs a specific title, an accurate description, a
self-consistent canonical, and a useful server-rendered introduction. Metadata
must describe visible behavior and actual availability. Avoid unsupported
customer counts, ratings, compliance claims, AI autonomy, or inferred features
from a retained route. A keyword tag does not replace useful content.

## Build content around actual workflows

A product guide explains purpose, access, the common workflow, outcomes,
limitations, and related products. Feature pages record scope, defaults,
exceptions, and regression evidence. Tutorials teach one reproducible task.
Reference pages identify contracts and versions. Troubleshooting pages map a
symptom to the owning boundary and observable evidence.

Use the [product directory](/platform/applications/overview),
[getting started](/platform/guides/getting-started),
[workflows](/platform/guides/workflows), and
[repository inventory](/reference/repository/catalog) as the content hubs.
Prefer substantive first-party explanations over automatically creating thin
pages for every keyword, API handler, query variant, or unsupported use case.
Generated route references locate source; they do not replace product tutorials.

## Localization and social discovery

Web and Nova public pages use unprefixed English and `/vi` Vietnamese URLs.
Distinct language pages need reciprocal hreflang and an English `x-default`.
Canonical URLs exclude tracking/search parameters. Public apps that use one
stable URL with locale preferences do not advertise fictitious translations.
Maintain user-visible metadata copy in both message bundles when adding strings.

Use the actual page/product title and description in Open Graph and Twitter
cards. Use valid absolute images and meaningful alt text. Private record names,
bearer tokens, emails, submitted answers, and hidden-case data must not leak into
public schemas, titles, or discovery feeds.

## Technical requirements

- Apply the [shared indexing policy](/platform/features/search-indexing) to every
  Next app and new route; default private routes to noindex.
- Keep sitemap URLs on the owning host. Include only canonical, indexable,
  successful content. Do not publish auth, order-token, cart, or checkout URLs.
- Use a publication-aware anonymous reader for dynamic discovery. An admin query
  or signed-in session must not expand a public sitemap.
- Use real publication/update timestamps for `lastmod`; omit it when no reliable
  timestamp exists. Do not mark every static page fresh on each request/build.
- Keep redirects and noindex responses crawlable so search engines can see them.
- Serve real 404s for missing published content, maintain redirect continuity for
  moved public pages, and avoid soft-404 success pages in sitemaps.
- Keep important copy and links in server HTML. Deferred interactive demos must
  not be the only explanation of a product.
- Use structured data only for actual visible entities. Organization/WebSite/
  WebPage/WebApplication can describe the platform; product, article, or other
  schemas require the corresponding real content and data. Do not fabricate
  reviews or expect a rich-result guarantee.
- Noindex preview/staging and inactive migration shells. Authentication and
  authorization remain independent of SEO.

## Measurement and review

For each verified release, inspect served headers, HTML, canonical/hreflang,
sitemap and robots responses, and publication/access edge cases. Submit the
owning public sitemaps through authorized Search Console/Bing accounts. Track:

| Measure | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical indexed public pages | Compare declared eligible pages with Google's selected canonical/status |
| Excluded private pages | Investigate any private route indexed or eligible unexpectedly |
| Impressions and clicks by intent/page | Discover gaps in copy, topics, and public page usefulness |
| Qualified app opens/onboarding | Connect discovery to an actual useful next step, with privacy-aware analytics |
| Documentation task completion | Use feedback/search failures to prioritize missing instructions |
| Crawl errors, redirects, and stale sitemaps | Find implementation/ownership drift |

Establish a baseline before interpreting changes. Compare the same window and
intent/page groups, accounting for release timing and seasonality. Search indexing
and ranking are external outcomes; passing code checks does not prove either.
Search Console account access, submission, and production deployment require
their own authorized delivery scope.

References: [Google developer SEO](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/get-started-developers),
[localized versions](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions),
and [sitemap guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/build-sitemap).
